speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual start; could you please clarify what symptoms you are experiencing or what medical history you would like me to review today? Specifically, are you presenting with issues regarding your gait, limb coordination, or balance?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To better understand the progression of your gait and limb ataxia, could you tell me if these symptoms started gradually or suddenly, and whether they have been worsening over time? Also, have you noticed any changes in your speech, vision, or swallowing difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, combined with new-onset gait and limb ataxia, you are at high risk for PML, a rare brain infection caused by the JC virus. I need to confirm this immediately with specific testing. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with and without contrast.
